To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutamate excitoxicity is the key molecular mechanisms that influence temperature-mediated brain damage during the acute phase.

glutamate excitotoxcity is the key mechanism which is influenced during brain stroke by body temperature, and that the modulation of glutamate excitotoxic damage by temperature is not dependent on the immune response to ischemic insult.
glutamate excitotoxy is the key molecular mechanisms which is influenced by temperature during the acute stage of brain stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms that underlie the influence of body temperature on the ischemic damage in the brain during the acute phase after stroke.
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the effects of body temperature on ischemic damage.
the understanding of the effects of temperature in the acute phase of ischemia, which is of clinical interest for stroke treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of temperature on ischemic damage in the acute phase of ischemic brain injury are mainly mediated by the modulation of glutamate excitotoxic effects, and to a lesser extend through the modulation of the metabolic rate and the inflammatory response.
temperature is a key factor that modulates glutamate excitotoxic effects during the acute phase after stroke.
the temperature-mediated deleterious effects on brain damage are due to a direct influence on glutamate excitotoxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deleterious and beneficial effects of body temperature during the first 24 hours after stroke are mainly mediated by glutamate excitotoxic damage.

the temperature-induced changes in glutamate excitotoxic mechanisms are the key molecular mechanisms which determine the deleterious effect of hyperthermia, and the beneficial effect of hypothermia during the acute phase after brain stroke.
glutamate excitotoxy is the key mechanism which influences the deleterious effect of hyperthermia, and the beneficial effect of hypothermia during the acute phase in ischemic brain damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deleterious and beneficial effects of hyperthermic and hypothermic temperatures during the acute phase are mainly mediated by glutamate excitotoxic effects.
the deleterious effect of hyperthermia on brain ischemia is mainly due to its influence on glutamate excitotoxic mechanisms.
glutamate excitoxicity is the key mechanism which is influenced during the acute phase by body temperature.
